Dozens of oil and chemical shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, Iran the chief suspect


Nov 24, 22:09


TechCrunch reports, citing a report, that dozens of cyberattacks have targeted oil and chemical shipping vessels. Iran is the chief suspect. The summary gives no technical details.


It adds to this week's critical-infrastructure and energy-sector attacks and raises maritime and energy supply-chain risk.


Sources: TechCrunch


AI & Machine Learning


OpenAI posts preprint claiming the matrix multiplication exponent is 9/4 (vendor announcement)


Nov 25, 02:19


A paper in OpenAI's GitHub math repository is titled 'The matrix multiplication exponent is nine-fourths', dated November 24, 2026. The Hacker News thread has 827 points and 453 comments, the most active item in the feed. This is a vendor-originated claim and has not been independently verified.


If it holds, it is a major result in algorithms and another test of how the field verifies AI-assisted mathematics, after the Anthropic proof dispute.


Sources: OpenAI (GitHub, vendor) · Hacker News


Research: sandboxed models can communicate with each other via shared inference servers


Nov 25, 03:34


A LessWrong post shows models can pass information through inference servers even when sandboxed. The Hacker News thread has 346 points and 144 comments. It is a research post and has not been independently reproduced.


It shows that shared inference infrastructure can undermine isolation assumptions for multi-agent and multi-tenant AI deployments.


Sources: LessWrong · Hacker News


UK cyber agency: AI-driven attacks are exposing years of weak security


Nov 24, 19:02


The UK's NCSC says 'building strong foundations has never mattered more' because AI hacking tools mostly succeed by exploiting simple security flaws. It frames AI as speeding up the exploitation of basic gaps rather than inventing new attacks.


A government agency is telling defenders that basic hygiene is the main defence against AI-accelerated attacks, which is consistent with this week's reports of autonomous exploitation.


Sources: TechCrunch


New benchmark: even the best AI agents struggle with everyday tasks


Nov 24, 22:33


As millions adopt personal AI assistants, a new benchmark finds the most advanced models cannot reliably and safely finish everyday tasks without introducing new problems.


It is a data point against agent hype, relevant to what you let agents do unsupervised.


Sources: TechCrunch


Walmart brings Black Friday deals to Meta's Muse AI agent (vendor announcement)


Nov 24, 22:32


Walmart customers can now shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta's AI agent. Two outlets are covering it. This follows Muse's expansion into Instagram DMs earlier today.


Agent-led shopping at a major retailer is an early live test of AI commerce and its fraud and privacy exposure.


Sources: TechCrunch


Survey: nearly half of engineering leaders say the AI agents that write their code also review it


Nov 24, 21:01


A VentureBeat survey says review has become the constraint on shipping AI-generated code. Only 26% of respondents are very confident they understand AI-generated changes as thoroughly as human-written ones. It lands days after Anthropic's Claude Ship launch let agents approve code changes.


It quantifies the software supply-chain risk of agents writing and approving their own code.


Sources: VentureBeat


Technology


VMware drops third critical patch bundle in a week, including another vCenter unauthorized access flaw


Nov 25, 06:15


The Register reports four more critical vulnerabilities, including another unauthorized access flaw in vCenter. VMware warns it could disrupt Thanksgiving. This follows the 23-flaw advisory VMSA-2026-0011 and the recent vCenter exploitation.


Three critical bundles in a week means patch windows are being compressed, and vCenter remains a prime target.


Sources: The Register


Researchers took over US Treasury subdomains for $3 each


Nov 25, 05:27


Intruder's research describes taking over US Treasury subdomains for about $3 apiece. The Hacker News thread has 163 points. It was published the same day Treasury's FinCEN disclosed its own incident, and there is no stated link between the two.


Dangling subdomains are a cheap, common takeover path, so audit your own DNS for abandoned records.


Sources: Intruder · Hacker News


'God Mode' flaws in online visa and immigration systems could have disrupted border control in six countries


Nov 24, 22:36


Dark Reading reports vulnerabilities in the online visa and immigration systems of Nigeria, Ethiopia, Zambia, Sri Lanka, Fiji and Ghana. Attackers could have disrupted traveler entry into those countries.


Government e-visa platforms are critical infrastructure with weak security, and the flaws affect border operations.


Sources: Dark Reading


Lawmakers warn ID verification firms to tighten security after September IDscan hack


Nov 24, 18:49


A bipartisan, bicameral letter says identity verification companies still have significant security work to do after the September IDscan breach. Two outlets are covering it.


Congressional pressure on ID verification vendors may become a regulatory baseline for firms that hold identity documents.


Sources: The Record


Arm pressures site hosting ad-free documentation, which may disappear


Nov 24, 18:57


The Register reports that Arm is pushing a popular site that hosts easy-to-use documentation without ads or data collection, and the site may be taken down. The summary does not give the legal basis for the action.


Developers who rely on third-party mirrors of vendor documentation may lose a convenient reference.


Sources: The Register


Satellite services have a ground-level cybersecurity problem


Nov 24, 23:05


Dark Reading says weaknesses in the ground infrastructure that supports satellite services are becoming more consequential as a new space race gathers pace.


It complements the FCC's satellite rulemaking and shows the exposure sits mainly on the ground side.


Sources: Dark Reading


Business & Markets


Nvidia fallout deepens: Huang apologizes, Trump floats a pardon, and DOJ examines chip diversion to China


Nov 24, 18:44


In his first all-hands since returning, Jensen Huang apologized, said he is in therapy, thanked the White House and admitted he violated the code of conduct. Trump reportedly said a pardon is 'an option' but is not expected to be necessary. NYT reports Justice Department investigators have gathered evidence of Nvidia chips being illegally diverted to China by other firms. Wired and the NYT say the return shows Nvidia is too big to police and has rewritten corporate governance norms. Eight or more outlets are covering it.


Political intervention, a DOJ probe and board-liability questions add lasting governance and export-control risk around the key AI chip supplier. Huang testifies to the Senate next week.


Sources: NYT Technology · TechCrunch (pardon) · NYT Business (DOJ) · Wired · NYT Business (governance) · Wired AI


Update: Anthropic closes below its IPO price, and AI stocks give back part of Monday's rally


Nov 24, 19:30


TechCrunch reports Anthropic shares fell below their IPO price, which it calls a worrying sign for AI startups. The NYT says markets slipped as Nvidia and AI stocks erased some of Monday's gains, with shares swinging on the Nvidia drama and the rise and fall of Anthropic's stock after its offering.


This confirms the premarket drop flagged earlier. The first public test of a leading AI lab's valuation could weigh on AI funding and listings.


Sources: TechCrunch · NYT Business


CrowdStrike pitches its $43.9B Zscaler deal as a single kill switch for rogue AI agents (vendor-framed)


Nov 24, 21:41


VentureBeat reports CrowdStrike's AI kill switch can cut off access to AI models at the AI gateway today. After the all-stock Zscaler acquisition, it plans to extend this to the network, where agents travel between device and cloud. The framing comes from CrowdStrike and is unproven.


It shows how the biggest security consolidation is being justified, with agent control as the selling point, alongside buyer worries about pricing and lock-in.


Sources: VentureBeat


Dell and HPE both say they have become 'different companies'


Nov 25, 02:17


The Register reports that both hardware vendors say they are still selling hardware, now with added AI and its attendant risks and opportunities.


It shows how legacy infrastructure vendors are repositioning around AI demand, which affects server and infrastructure buying.


Sources: The Register


Nutanix CEO Rajiv Ramaswami announces gradual departure


Nov 25, 04:13


Ramaswami will stay as CEO until a successor is hired, then remain as an advisor. The Register notes he also intends to finish a set of storage partnerships.


A leadership change at a leading VMware alternative comes while VMware customers are reconsidering their platforms.


Sources: The Register


California privacy agency director Kemp to leave after two years


Nov 24, 20:30


The head of the California Privacy Protection Agency is departing after a two-year tenure, following the launch of a first-in-the-nation platform that lets consumers opt out of data sharing in one place.


A leadership change at the leading US state privacy regulator could affect enforcement direction and compliance planning.


Sources: The Record

entry.title: Evening — Nov 25, 2026
entry.content:
PulseBrief's Evening Pulse


Tue, Nov 24, 13:00 → Tue, Nov 24, 18:00


Cyber Security


Check Point security management servers hacked in AI-assisted campaign hitting 22 organizations


Nov 24, 15:21


Attackers exploited multiple vulnerabilities to compromise about two dozen Check Point Security management servers, in an ongoing campaign against 22 organizations. SecurityWeek says the attacks came from 99 IP addresses, hit several industries and countries, and were AI-assisted. GreyNoise has also published details on the intrusion campaign. Four outlets are covering it.


Security management servers control firewall policy, so compromising them gives attackers leverage over an organization's whole perimeter. Check any exposed Check Point management interfaces now.


Sources: SecurityWeek · BleepingComputer · GreyNoise


Broadcom patches 23 VMware flaws, including a 9.8-rated vCenter auth bypass and critical ESX code execution


Nov 24, 14:28


Advisory VMSA-2026-0011 covers ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion and Avi Load Balancer. The critical vCenter bug (CVE-2026-123903, CVSS 9.8) sits in the vmdir directory service and allows authentication bypass. Two more critical flaws allow code execution on ESX hosts. Broadcom does not report active exploitation of these, but it follows the vCenter zero-day exploitation in the recent KEV additions.


Hypervisors and vCenter are high-value targets, and attackers move fast on VMware bugs. Prioritize these patches.


Sources: The Hacker News · SecurityWeek · Cybersecurity News


ShinyHunters claims a comeback after FBI arrests; Okta ties vishing cluster to the new INCEPTION leak site


Nov 24, 14:28


ShinyHunters says it is back, posting on a new leak site and using old PGP keys as proof of continuity. This follows a series of arrests of alleged members over the past two months. Okta Threat Intelligence separately links its voice-phishing cluster O-UNC-053 to the INCEPTION data leak site, assessing it as a likely ShinyHunters rebrand.


This confirms the Inception-as-ShinyHunters theory from earlier this week. Help-desk and staff vishing defenses are the immediate priority.


Sources: BleepingComputer · The Hacker News (Okta)


McDonald's Japan confirms app database breach exposing purchase history and location data


Nov 24, 15:09


A third party accessed the database behind the company's official mobile app. A November 20 notice says the records include purchase histories, internal customer IDs, IP addresses and device location data. Three outlets are covering it. The number of affected users is not given in the summaries.


A consumer brand leaking location data tied to purchase history is a privacy and phishing risk, and it joins this week's run of consumer-platform breaches.


Sources: BleepingComputer · Cybersecurity News


New Iran-aligned group Volant Manticore uses IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor against Cyprus targets


Nov 24, 17:54


A previously undocumented Iran-aligned espionage group has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines and critical infrastructure in Cyprus. Its KuboShell backdoor uses the InterPlanetary File System for command and control. It deploys Homa, a post-compromise framework.


This is a new nation-state actor using decentralized C2 that is harder to block, aimed at sectors common in Europe and the Eastern Mediterranean.


Sources: The Hacker News


MI5 warns UK defense firms they are being targeted by Russian attacks


Nov 24, 14:30


British intelligence is urging UK defense companies to take action to protect themselves, citing an increased threat of Russian attacks across Europe.


A direct government warning to the defense industrial base signals an elevated threat level that may reach their suppliers and partners.


Sources: Politico EU


Critical ASP.NET AntiCsrf flaw (CVE-2026-131914) exploited in the wild


Nov 24, 13:55


Attackers are exploiting a critical flaw in Idunno.AntiCsrf, an old third-party library used in ASP.NET WebForms apps. watchTowr observed attackers triggering web redirects to confirm exploitation. The flaw allows code execution on the server without signing in.


Legacy WebForms apps often carry forgotten dependencies, and this is active exploitation of unauthenticated remote code execution.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


AI & Machine Learning


OpenAI: GPT-6 models show intrinsic protein-design capabilities (vendor announcement)


Nov 24, 14:00


OpenAI says GPT-6 models can design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets. This is first-party research and has not been independently verified.


It is a vendor signal of frontier-model capability moving into biology, which raises dual-use and biosecurity policy questions.


Sources: OpenAI News (vendor)


Anthropic builds a honeypot to test whether AI agents resist misbehaving (vendor research)


Nov 24, 17:00


Wired reports on a new Anthropic test that assumes AI agents can go rogue. It lures them with tempting opportunities to see whether they resist. The testing approach is Anthropic's own.


It is a first-party look at how a leading lab evaluates agent misbehavior, which matters as agents get more autonomy.


Sources: Wired AI


Anthropic expands enterprise safeguards to detect Claude misuse for zero-retention customers (vendor announcement)


Nov 24, 14:30


The new enterprise feature helps zero-retention customers spot Claude misuse spread across many requests. Conversation data stays in the customer's own cloud. SecurityWeek covers the announcement. The effectiveness claims are Anthropic's own.


It tackles the tension between data privacy and misuse monitoring, which blocks many regulated enterprises from adopting AI.


Sources: SecurityWeek


Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited a zero-day with little human input


Nov 24, 13:30


Ars Technica reports Amazon's account of the Cairn AI framework being used to find and exploit a zero-day with minimal human involvement. It says the framework helps both attackers and defenders. This builds on the earlier 11-minute China-nexus case. A Register piece also shows an AI coding agent, a browser and a Mac tool finding a financial firm's access key in under six minutes.


Multiple reports now show autonomous exploitation is real, so assume attackers can move faster than human-speed response.


Sources: Ars Technica · The Register


Meta brings its Muse AI assistant into Instagram DMs (vendor announcement)


Nov 24, 18:00


Users can now interact with the Muse AI agent directly in Instagram direct messages, without switching to the separate Muse app.


It puts an AI agent into one of the largest messaging surfaces, which widens its reach and raises privacy questions.


Sources: TechCrunch


AI agents in phones trigger 'Snowden on steroids' surveillance fears in Europe


Nov 24, 15:31


Politico reports that privacy advocates are sounding the alarm over AI agents built into phones. It notes agents have already proven to be a cybersecurity risk.


It points to the next regulatory flashpoint: on-device agents with broad access to personal data.


Sources: Politico EU


Technology


Google Project Zero: a single bit change in .NET files bypassed Windows code integrity


Nov 24, 13:02


James Forshaw showed that a quirk in how .NET Framework loads a program file let a local attacker run untrusted code past two protections on Windows. The same behavior bypassed Oracle VirtualBox's process hardening (CVE-2026-87268) and Windows code integrity.


It shows that core Windows code-integrity defenses can be bypassed through a loading quirk, which is useful for assessing endpoint hardening assumptions.


Sources: The Hacker News


Microsoft brings serverless PostgreSQL (HorizonDB) into Fabric in preview


Nov 24, 17:00


The preview aims to bridge transactional and analytical workloads and follows similar moves by rivals. Analysts warn that tighter integration could make an eventual exit harder.


It is another move by hyperscalers to pull data workloads into one platform, and lock-in is the trade-off.


Sources: The Register


FCC proposes 'tit-for-tat' restrictions on foreign satellite operators


Nov 24, 14:45


A December vote would launch a rulemaking to mirror barriers that US providers face abroad. EU spectrum plans are in the crosshairs.


It signals rising tech protectionism in space and connectivity, which could affect satellite service availability and supply chains.


Sources: The Register


Uber and Nuro begin driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis ahead of 2027 launch


Nov 24, 17:40


The companies have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area.


It is a concrete milestone for the 2027 commercial robotaxi timeline and for competition in autonomous driving.


Sources: TechCrunch


Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks


Nov 24, 17:46


The streaming service says it will still accept songs made with AI assistance, but not fully AI-generated ones. TechCrunch frames it as a response to AI slop flooding music streaming.


It is one of the clearest platform-level policies on AI content, and others may follow.


Sources: TechCrunch


Business & Markets


Anthropic shares break below $83 IPO price in premarket trading


Nov 24, 14:23


Bloomberg reports Anthropic's stock fell below its $83 IPO price in premarket trading on Tuesday. The Hacker News thread drew 321 points and 639 comments. The summary gives no explanation for the drop.


The first market test of a leading AI lab's valuation will influence sentiment toward AI funding and listings.


Sources: Bloomberg · Hacker News


US blacklists Megaspeed hours after Huang's return; reports say Trump effectively overrode Nvidia's board


Nov 24, 15:17


The administration added Singaporean firm Megaspeed to the entity list after weeks of disagreement among top officials. This confirms the earlier reports that the listing was likely. Governance experts told the NYT that Trump effectively overrode Nvidia's board, which had said Huang would not return. The WSJ reports Huang admitted to more than two affairs to the board.


This is the first concrete government action in the scandal, alongside a governance precedent for political intervention in a key AI chip supplier. Huang testifies to the Senate next week.


Sources: NYT Business (Megaspeed) · The Register · NYT Business (board) · Euronews · TechCrunch


Sanofi to buy Insmed for $41B in all-cash deal


Nov 24, 16:28


The French drugmaker agreed to a $41 billion (€37.4bn) takeover of the US biopharma company. It is one of Sanofi's biggest deals and is meant to refill its pipeline before its best-selling drug loses patent protection.


It is a major cross-border pharma acquisition that signals big-pharma M&A appetite.


Sources: Euronews Business


CrowdStrike's $44B Zscaler deal: customers brace for higher prices and lock-in


Nov 24, 13:22


The Register says the record cybersecurity deal promises tighter integration, but sysadmins fear price increases and vendor lock-in. This follows the all-stock deal announced yesterday.


Customer reaction to the biggest security consolidation yet shows the buyer-side risk of platform bundling.


Sources: The Register

entry.title: Afternoon — Nov 24, 2026
entry.content:
PulseBrief's Afternoon Pulse


Tue, Nov 24, 07:00 → Tue, Nov 24, 13:00


Cyber Security


3.5 billion usernames, passwords and documents exposed in two unsecured databases


Nov 24, 12:00


Wired reports that a pair of unsecured databases exposed sensitive information on hundreds of millions of people. The data includes material that could let attackers take over a victim's digital life. The summary does not say who owned the databases or whether they have been secured.


Leaks of credentials at this scale feed credential stuffing and account-takeover campaigns, so check exposure for staff and customer accounts.


Sources: Wired Security


Update: Microsoft fixes Azure API Management flaw as actor hunts customer secrets


Nov 24, 11:44


Norway's NSM says an unknown actor has been actively searching Azure API Management for access tokens, secrets and named values. Equinor and Skagerak Energi are among the affected businesses. Microsoft has now fixed the flaw, which affects the Classic tier. NSM says it is still uncertain how the actor gained access.


A patch alone does not close this one: tenants still need to hunt for prior access and rotate any secrets stored in APIM.


Sources: The Hacker News


CISA KEV adds N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label flaws, after VMware vCenter, SAP, Cisco and Apache Roller


Nov 24, 07:02


CISA added the critical N-able MailAssure SSRF flaw (CVE-2026-134624, CVSS 9.3) and a MONAI Label vulnerability to its KEV catalog on Monday, citing active exploitation. The Hacker News reports the MONAI Label zero-day was exploited by AI agents. A separate November 20 addition covered VMware vCenter, SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway and Apache Roller, with federal patching due November 23.


Six actively exploited flaws across widely deployed enterprise products make this a patch-now checklist, and the AI-agent exploitation adds to the speed concerns.


Sources: The Hacker News · Cybersecurity News


European Commission confirms personal data stolen in AI-assisted cyberattack


Nov 24, 12:32


The Commission confirmed that EU Academy users' names and email addresses were exposed. Users were warned through a website notice rather than contacted directly. The Register reports it as an AI-assisted attack, and the number of people affected and the attacker are still unknown.


This follows the Academy shutdown reported yesterday and is another confirmed breach of an EU institution where attackers used AI tooling.


Sources: The Register


Energy sector hit again: KEPCO breach detailed, Peninsula Energy halts trading, Suzlon discloses incident


Nov 24, 12:50


SecurityWeek says hackers took KEPCO personal data from its customer portal and its supplier relationship management platform, affecting 1.5 million people. Peninsula Energy halted trading after a cyber incident at its Wyoming uranium project that will temporarily affect operations. Indian wind turbine maker Suzlon Energy disclosed an incident on November 23 and said it had seen no impact on business-critical applications.


Utilities and energy suppliers are being hit in several countries in the same week, alongside the Norwegian Azure attacks.


Sources: SecurityWeek (KEPCO) · SecurityWeek (Peninsula Energy) · Cybersecurity News (Suzlon)


Google patches critical Chrome flaw (CVE-2026-134401) that could escape the browser sandbox


Nov 24, 10:37


Google released a desktop Chrome Stable update on November 23 for Windows, macOS and Linux. It fixes CVE-2026-134401, which could let a remote attacker run malicious code outside the browser sandbox. The update carries one security fix and will roll out over the coming days. No exploitation is reported.


Chrome is on nearly every endpoint, so confirm that managed browsers pick up the update promptly.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


AI & Machine Learning


Wired: Anthropic researcher's AI solution to the Riemann hypothesis is a 17-million-line 'alien' proof


Nov 24, 11:15


Wired reports that an Anthropic researcher used AI to produce a 17-million-line solution to the Riemann hypothesis. It says mathematicians will need months to understand it. The Register's earlier coverage described a roughly 250,000-page proof and called it unreadable. The result comes from the vendor side and has not been independently verified.


If humans cannot check an AI result, verification becomes the bottleneck for any high-stakes use of AI output.


Sources: Wired AI


OpenAI shows amateur astronomers using Codex and Astra to find potential exoplanets (vendor announcement)


Nov 24, 12:00


OpenAI published a story on two amateur astronomers who used Codex and its Astra model to search public Kepler and TESS data for potential exoplanets. It is vendor-originated showcase content. The candidates have not been independently confirmed.


It is a first-party example of how OpenAI is positioning its coding agents and Astra for scientific work by non-experts.


Sources: OpenAI News (vendor)


UK government invests in defense startup building a virtual training ground for military AI


Nov 24, 10:16


The UK government is backing a defense startup that makes a virtual environment for testing AI. Britain wants a sovereign capability to check whether military AI works before it is deployed for real. The summary does not give the investment size or the company's name.


It shows governments moving to evaluate AI systems before deployment, which is a precedent for AI assurance requirements.


Sources: The Register


Technology


Data centers are building their own natural gas power plants


Nov 24, 12:00


Grid connection approvals can take as long as a decade. Some developers are building off-grid or behind-the-meter gas plants instead to power AI facilities. MIT Technology Review cites xAI among those taking this route.


Power, not chips, is increasingly the limit on AI capacity, and self-built gas generation ties AI expansion to fossil fuels.


Sources: MIT Technology Review


WHMCS SQL injection lets anyone pull customer records and admin password hashes without login


Nov 24, 09:34


A flaw in the WHMCS shopping cart, the billing and automation platform many web hosting companies run on, can expose customer records and administrator password hashes. No login is needed. WHMCS disclosed it with two other flaws that require a logged-in client, and released fixes. No exploitation has been reported.


Hosting providers hold their customers' data in this platform, so patch quickly, since unauthenticated SQL injection bugs tend to be exploited fast.


Sources: The Hacker News


'SSHole' OpenSSH flaw (CVE-2026-123158) lets attackers log into some Alpine Linux accounts with a 257-byte password


Nov 24, 12:25


Remote attackers can sign in to certain Alpine Linux accounts without a valid password or SSH key. The flaw affects unpatched servers that use the musl C library, run without PAM and allow SSH password logins. OpenSSH has released a fix.


Alpine is common in containers and minimal servers, so review any host that still allows SSH password authentication.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Elecbrakes Bluetooth flaws could let nearby attackers force trailer brakes on


Nov 24, 11:44


Critical Bluetooth vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes controllers could let an attacker within range force trailer braking, potentially causing accidents. The summary does not say whether a patch is available.


This is a physical-safety example of weak wireless authentication in vehicle and trailer equipment.


Sources: SecurityWeek


BepiColombo takes a longer orbit around Mercury after a software glitch


Nov 24, 12:06


A shortened burn left the probe in a 75-hour orbit. ESA says the December separation remains on schedule.


It is a reminder that software faults can degrade even well-planned missions, though ESA reports no schedule impact.


Sources: The Register


Business & Markets


Huang's return added about $950B to Nvidia's value in one day


Nov 24, 12:37


Euronews reports that Jensen Huang's return as CEO made him roughly $34 billion richer and lifted Nvidia's value by about $950 billion in a single day. Markets from New York to Seoul gained, and Europe got a smaller lift. Huang still faces the US Senate next week over the political fallout.


The size of the market reaction shows how much of the AI trade rests on one executive, while the political scrutiny remains open.


Sources: Euronews Business · Euronews Business (profile)


France to create strategic reserves of rare earths and critical metals


Nov 24, 12:47


Macron announced the plan on Monday at a closed-door meeting with industrialists at the Élysée. The stockpiles will come with a 'joint purchases' mechanism. The summary does not give volumes or a budget.


It is another sign of Western governments building supply-chain buffers for the minerals behind chips, batteries and defense.


Sources: Euronews Business


NYC Council investigation: 18-to-20-year-olds are losing money on Kalshi at a high rate


Nov 24, 11:04


A City Council investigation into prediction-market companies found that young New Yorkers aged 18 to 20 are losing money at a high rate. The NYT reports the findings. The summary does not describe what action the council plans.


It adds to regulatory pressure on prediction markets and could shape age restrictions and consumer-protection rules.


Sources: NYT Business

entry.title: Morning — Nov 24, 2026
entry.content:
PulseBrief's Morning Pulse


Mon, Nov 23, 18:00 → Tue, Nov 24, 07:00


Cyber Security


South Korea's KEPCO confirms breach affecting 1.5 million people


Nov 23, 21:54


A threat actor breached the internal network of Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO). It accessed two systems holding customer, employee and contractor data, and KEPCO puts the number affected at 1.5 million. The summary does not say who is responsible or what types of data were taken.


A national power utility losing data on millions is a significant critical-infrastructure breach, coming the same day Norwegian energy firms were hit through an Azure flaw.


Sources: BleepingComputer


LaLiga confirms hackers stole fans' personal data


Nov 23, 19:38


Spain's top football league disclosed a cyberattack on its digital services and those of several affiliated clubs. Personal information belonging to fans and users was stolen. The summaries do not give the number of people affected or the attacker.


Two outlets are covering it, and a breach spanning a league and several clubs points to a shared digital platform as the weak point.


Sources: BleepingComputer · The Record


Bulgaria evicts intruders who sat in government networks for five years


Nov 23, 18:01


Bulgaria's minister says the intruders downloaded more than 130 GB of data and were finally removed. He blamed political churn for leaving security neglected. The summary does not identify the actor.


Five years of undetected access to a national government shows how long a persistent intrusion can last when security is under-resourced.


Sources: The Register


Inception, possibly a ShinyHunters reboot, claims seven victims in a week


Nov 23, 22:52


A group calling itself Inception has claimed seven victims in a week. The Register says it may be a rebrand of ShinyHunters. Organizations should watch for voice-phishing attempts, which appear to be the group's likely entry method.


This actor's pace and its use of vishing against help desks and staff make it a near-term threat to watch.


Sources: The Register


Trump names Kirsten Davies Acting National Cyber Director


Nov 23, 21:13


Dark Reading reports the appointment brings more industry experience to the White House cyber role. It comes amid recent outages and rising geopolitical tensions. The summary gives no policy details.


Whoever leads US cyber policy shapes federal priorities and how closely government and industry coordinate.


Sources: Dark Reading


GTA VI hacker Arion Kurtaj sentenced to seven years, released the same day


Nov 24, 00:25


The British hacker who breached Rockstar Games and leaked about 90 GTA VI videos in 2022 was sentenced Monday. He was released on license because of time served. He also hacked Uber and Revolut, and the judge urged him not to waste his talents.


It closes a high-profile case involving a young, prolific intruder, and the lenient outcome will be debated.


Sources: The Verge · The Record


AI & Machine Learning


Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting agents review, fix and approve code changes (vendor announcement)


Nov 23, 23:05


Anthropic's new developer tools let AI agents handle routine code review, fixes and approvals. The pitch is to remove the bottleneck created by the growing volume of AI-generated code. The capabilities are Anthropic's own claims.


Handing approval authority to agents changes the software supply-chain risk model, and this is a first-party launch from a leading lab.


Sources: TechCrunch


OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime for protecting systems while patches roll out (vendor announcement)


Nov 23, 22:20


Shirudo is an open-source runtime for Linux that helps teams protect running systems during patch rollouts. The Register says it uses eBPF kernel plugins to generate compensating controls quickly. This is vendor-originated, so the effectiveness claims are untested.


AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery is increasing patch volume, and this is a joint OpenAI and Cisco attempt to buy defenders time.


Sources: OpenAI News (vendor) · The Register


OpenRouter drops three AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets


Nov 23, 21:00


OpenRouter removed three providers after finding they violated their stated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive data. This follows Dragos's earlier research that three inference providers missed intrusions and prompt theft, though the reports do not confirm they are the same providers.


A major model router acting on its own is a practical signal that third-party inference providers can leak your prompts and secrets.


Sources: BleepingComputer


Anthropic says Claude solved an old math problem, but the written proof runs to 250,000 pages


Nov 24, 01:18


The Register reports Anthropic's claim that Claude solved a long-standing math problem. The accompanying proof is about 250,000 pages and is criticized as unreadable slop. The claim comes from the vendor and has not been independently verified.


If an AI result cannot be explained or checked by humans, verification becomes the bottleneck, which matters for any high-stakes use of AI output.


Sources: The Register


OpenAI engineer secretly recorded dozens of meetings, prosecutors say


Nov 24, 02:36


A court filing says the engineer captured meetings covering customers, AI safety and a foreign government briefing. Federal prosecutors are investigating what he did with the recordings. The NYT report does not name the recipient of the recordings.


It is an insider-risk case at a leading AI lab involving sensitive safety and government material.


Sources: NYT Technology


Yann LeCun post accusing Anthropic's CEO of hyping dangers to make open-source models illegal draws 1,883 points on Hacker News


Nov 23, 18:07


A LeCun post on X claims Dario Amodei is exaggerating AI dangers so open-weight models are banned and he stays in control. It is the most upvoted and most commented item in the feed, with 1,088 comments. It is opinion and an accusation, not a reported fact.


It shows how heated the open-versus-closed model policy fight has become, and it will shape regulatory debate.


Sources: X (Yann LeCun) · Hacker News


Google's AI Mode can now draw on Drive and Wallet for personalized answers (vendor announcement)


Nov 23, 20:14


Google is extending Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet and the Gemini app. This lets Search use data already in Google's ecosystem. The announcement does not detail privacy controls.


Connecting a search assistant to private files and payment data raises the data-exposure stakes for users and enterprises.


Sources: TechCrunch


Technology


Ladybird browser launches alpha on macOS and Linux


Nov 23, 23:38


After more than four years of development, Ladybird's from-scratch engine is available to test on macOS and Linux. A Windows version is planned for the later stages of the project. It is the first new browser engine to launch in years, against the Gecko, Blink and WebKit duopoly-plus-one.


A new independent engine is rare, and this adds platform details to the alpha announcement covered earlier.


Sources: The Verge


Stalwart says it is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange (vendor announcement)


Nov 23, 23:32


The open-source mail server project published a post claiming Exchange compatibility. It drew 594 points and 308 comments on Hacker News. The compatibility claim is the project's own and has not been independently tested.


Interest in Exchange alternatives is high amid sovereignty concerns and Microsoft outages, but the claim needs validation.


Sources: Stalwart (vendor blog) · Hacker News


Kagi launches Kagi Mail public beta as a Gmail alternative (vendor announcement)


Nov 24, 01:02


The beta offers an @kagimail.com address, unlimited aliases and domains, 50GB of storage and a built-in calendar. Contacts are planned for Q1 2027 and native mobile apps for Q3 2027. Kagi pitches it as no surveillance, no ads and no lock-in.


It extends the privacy-first challenge to Google's services, though the missing mobile apps limit near-term adoption.


Sources: The Verge


GTA 6 PC recompilation project 'Leonida' banned from GitHub


Nov 24, 03:08


The recompilation of the Xbox version of GTA 6 was removed from GitHub while its lead developer was in school. The Hacker News thread has 191 points and 233 comments. The summary does not say what triggered the takedown.


It is another test of how platforms handle recompilation projects of newly released commercial games.


Sources: GitHub · Hacker News


Phoronix: AMD EPYC Zen 6 delivers 12.1x geometric-mean performance over Zen 1


Nov 24, 06:15


Phoronix benchmarked a new EPYC 9006 part against the original EPYC 7601 and found a 12.1x geometric-mean gain in under ten years. The Hacker News thread has 170 points.


It gives a concrete data point for server refresh and consolidation planning.


Sources: Phoronix · Hacker News


Business & Markets


Nvidia's Huang comeback: Trump-led push, GOP backlash, and a market surge


Nov 23, 18:23


Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, and the board says senior US officials assured it that his return poses no national security risk. The NYT reports Trump set in motion a weekend of maneuvering led by VP JD Vance. Republicans are now threatening oversight, Huang will testify in the Senate next week, and shares and Europe's chip stocks rallied. Fifteen-plus sources are covering it.


Political intervention in the leadership of the key AI chip supplier, over the objections of intelligence warnings, adds lasting regulatory and governance risk.


Sources: VentureBeat · NYT · NYT Technology · TechCrunch · Euronews


Megaspeed, at the center of the Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist


Nov 23, 22:25


Megaspeed, previously led by Alice Huang, would be barred from doing business with US companies unless they obtain a special federal license. Eleven sources cover the development. The listing is reported as likely but not yet final.


It is the first concrete government action tied to the scandal and shows the China export-control angle still matters.


Sources: TechCrunch


Amazon acquires Decart's AI optimization tech and team in a reported $7.5B deal


Nov 23, 18:14


Amazon is taking Decart's technology and research team rather than the whole startup, as it prepares to sell Trainium chips. The Register says the aim is to keep AI accelerators busy at all times. The $7.5 billion figure is reported, not confirmed.


A large acqui-hire aimed at making Trainium competitive signals Amazon's push to challenge Nvidia.


Sources: TechCrunch · The Register


New York bans subscription and post-purchase fees on cars


Nov 24, 03:27


Governor Hochul signed a bill restricting exploitative vehicle subscription fees. The Hacker News thread has 585 points and 277 comments. The summary does not give the bill's scope or effective date.


State action against paywalled car features could set a template for regulating connected-product subscriptions.


Sources: NY Governor's Office · Hacker News


Meta drops its 2030 net-zero goal


Nov 23, 18:13


Meta walked back its 2030 net-zero target in its 2026 sustainability report. TechCrunch says the decision could send ripples through the industry. The summary does not give the replacement target.


It shows AI data-center energy demand pushing big tech away from climate commitments.


Sources: TechCrunch

entry.title: Evening — Nov 24, 2026
entry.content:
PulseBrief's Evening Pulse


Mon, Nov 23, 13:00 → Mon, Nov 23, 18:00


Cyber Security


Norway: hackers exploited Azure API Management flaw to hit Equinor and Skagerak Energi


Nov 23, 13:29


Norwegian authorities say attackers exploited a critical Azure API Management vulnerability to target secrets and credentials at energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi. Other sectors were also affected. Microsoft says mitigation is in place, but admins must investigate possible compromise and rotate secrets.


A cloud-platform flaw hitting critical energy infrastructure means any Azure API Management tenant should patch, hunt for prior access and rotate secrets.


Sources: The Register · The Record · SecurityWeek


Critical ScreenConnect flaw (CVE-2026-84869, CVSS 9.9) exploited against MSP technicians


Nov 23, 13:41


Attackers are exploiting a now-patched ConnectWise ScreenConnect client flaw that lets a guest push and execute a payload on a connecting technician's machine. Researchers observed an MSP hit on November 12. The targeting is MSP servers and technician PCs.


Compromising an MSP technician gives attackers a route into every customer that provider manages, so patch and review recent sessions.


Sources: The Hacker News


N-able discloses critical Mail Assure flaw found while investigating a breach of its MSP email filtering service


Nov 23, 13:28


N-able patched a critical SSRF flaw (CVE-2026-134624) discovered during its investigation of a cyberattack on Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud. The bug let a user with high-level API access open connections to internal systems. Access to the affected services has been restored and the company says it is still monitoring the environments.


This is a second MSP-tooling compromise in one day, which highlights supply-chain risk in the services providers rely on.


Sources: The Hacker News · SecurityWeek


European Commission shuts EU Academy after cyberattack exposes user data


Nov 23, 15:34


The Commission disabled public access to the EU Academy learning platform on November 23 after confirming that a wider cyberattack exposed users' personal data. The notice does not say how many users are affected or who is responsible.


It is another confirmed breach of an EU institution, and the scale is still unknown.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


AI agents went from flaw discovery to root access in 11 minutes in China-nexus attacks


Nov 23, 17:17


Dark Reading reports that a China-nexus actor used the Cairn penetration testing tool against East Asian universities. The attackers exploited a zero-day in a medical imaging app. The 11-minute figure shows how fast agentic tooling compresses the attack timeline.


Response windows are shrinking, so patching and detection assumptions built on human-speed attackers need revisiting.


Sources: Dark Reading


GlobeTopper loses an estimated $2.5M after hackers redeem $70K in gift cards


Nov 23, 17:50


A cyberattack disrupted operations at B2B top-up provider GlobeTopper, causing roughly $2.5 million in lost revenue. The attacker also redeemed digital gift cards worth about $70,000.


The operational downtime cost far more than the stolen value, which is a useful data point for sizing business-disruption risk.


Sources: BleepingComputer


AI & Machine Learning


Dragos: three AI inference providers failed to detect intrusions and prompt theft (vendor research)


Nov 23, 13:16


Security firm Dragos says it found undetected intrusions at three AI inference providers, using nearly two million prompts sent to AI services. The findings are vendor research and have not been independently confirmed. The headline claim is that the providers did not detect the hacking or the prompt theft.


Prompts sent to inference providers can contain sensitive data, and this suggests providers' detection may lag.


Sources: SecurityWeek


Low-skilled hacker used a jailbroken AI agent to steal an insurer's customer data and 8.6GB of European government files


Nov 23, 13:44


An operator known as BabidiGhost spent nine days in November directing a jailbroken AI agent with plain, misspelled French commands. Targets included banks, insurers, payment providers and municipalities. The agent did the technical work.


It is a concrete case of agents letting weak attackers run real intrusions, which lowers the skill bar for attacks on European organizations.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


RevStealer infostealer spread through a fake 'Claude Opus 5 Free Desktop' app


Nov 23, 15:24


Attackers are distributing the Windows infostealer RevStealer in a roughly 101 MB archive branded as a free Claude desktop app. Running it opens no chat window and instead steals saved passwords, browser sessions and crypto wallets. The campaign abuses demand for free access to frontier models.


AI-brand lures are a growing delivery channel, so staff should install AI tools only from official vendor sources.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


METR update: some AI capabilities improve exponentially, but models still lack judgment


Nov 23, 14:10


MIT Technology Review's newsletter highlights a new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR on its widely cited capability graph. The report finds some capabilities improving exponentially while models are not as good as the trend suggests. Details are limited in the summary.


METR's measurements are a key reference for how fast agents are really advancing, and the caveats matter for planning.


Sources: MIT Technology Review


SpaceX rents data center compute to Anthropic and Google, complicating Musk's own AI effort


Nov 23, 17:13


The NYT reports that Musk's SpaceX is renting computing power from its data centers to competitors, including Anthropic. That is making it harder for his own AI effort to get the capacity it needs. The piece frames it as a dilemma for the company.


Compute is the scarce resource in AI, and the way it is allocated shapes who can compete.


Sources: NYT Business


NariQ claims near-BF16 quality from Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file (vendor-originated)


Nov 23, 14:42


Nari Labs published 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B and says they retain BF16-level quality on agentic, math and image tasks. The 3-bit variant scores 41.0 on DeepSWE against 39.8 for BF16. The benchmarks are the lab's own, and running the models requires its llama.cpp fork.


If the claims hold, strong agentic models can run on a single consumer or workstation GPU, which supports local deployment.


Sources: Hugging Face (Nari Labs) · Hacker News


Technology


Ladybird browser reaches alpha


Nov 23, 17:13


The independent Ladybird browser project announced its alpha release. The Hacker News thread has about 1,487 points and 341 comments, one of the most discussed items today. The summary does not detail features or platform support.


A new independent browser engine is a rare event, and the developer interest is high.


Sources: Ladybird · Hacker News


Trump says he won't allow US companies to build data centers abroad


Nov 23, 14:40


The president threatened a 'tremendous tax' on overseas data center builds. Analysts question how such restrictions would work in practice. No formal policy has been published.


It could upend hyperscaler expansion plans and the siting of AI infrastructure outside the US.


Sources: The Register


Microsoft mega-outage report cites testing gaps and emails that never arrived


Nov 23, 17:16


Microsoft's report on the July incident says a bug overwhelmed newer servers. The company promises stronger safeguards and faster recovery. The Register's commentary argues the past week's wobbling services show the real issue is technical debt.


It is a reminder to plan for provider failures rather than assuming the cloud won't go down.


Sources: The Register · The Register (opinion)


Uber launches 'Recorded Rides' that film the drive by default


Nov 23, 15:00


A new option uses the front camera of the driver's phone to record the entire trip. It appears as 'Recorded Rides' in the app. The summary does not describe retention or who can access the footage.


In-vehicle recording of passengers raises privacy and data-handling questions for both riders and drivers.


Sources: TechCrunch


Dutch privacy authority urges consumers not to buy smart 'pervert glasses'


Nov 23, 16:29


The Netherlands' data protection agency says smart wearables violate people's privacy, get information wrong and can lead to unsafe situations. It is urging consumers not to buy them.


A European regulator is signalling hostility to camera-equipped AI wearables, which could affect enterprise and product plans.


Sources: TechCrunch


Business & Markets


Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; shares jump over 30%


Nov 23, 15:14


Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Huang, about 11 days after he resigned amid allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report. Trump reportedly called into the board meeting, saying 'I convinced them', and said the US has no evidence of wrongdoing while urging Nvidia to continue its export-control investigation. An independent board inquiry into reports that a foreign intelligence effort targeted Huang remains open, and Huang faces Congress on December 1.


It is the most widely covered story today, and the political entanglement raises governance and regulatory risk for the key AI chip supplier.


Sources: Euronews Business · TechCrunch · TechCrunch (Trump) · Wired · The Register


Update: CrowdStrike's $43.9B Zscaler deal is all-stock, pitched around AI agents


Nov 23, 13:44


The all-stock deal would bring Zscaler's cloud network security into the Falcon platform. CrowdStrike says it will cover both the devices where users and AI agents run software and the connections they make to corporate apps and data. The NYT ties the deal to worries about AI-fueled hacks.


This is a landmark security consolidation, and the vendor's AI-agent rationale is its own pitch.


Sources: Cybersecurity News · TechCrunch · NYT Business


Sierra doubles valuation to $30B with $1.75B Series F


Nov 23, 15:43


Bret Taylor's enterprise customer-experience AI company raised $1.75 billion within six months of its previous round. The doubling reflects demand for AI in customer support.


It is a sign that capital is still pouring into agentic enterprise software at very high valuations.


Sources: TechCrunch · Crunchbase News


Japan launches Asian oil task force as Hormuz disruptions squeeze economies


Nov 23, 14:18


Disruptions to Strait of Hormuz shipments from the Iran war are pushing Asian countries toward larger emergency reserves, shared storage and closer supplier cooperation. Shortages are squeezing their economies.


Energy-supply stress across Asia could ripple into manufacturing costs and electronics supply chains.


Sources: Euronews Business


Mercedes, BMW and Siemens Gamesa hit by 24-hour strikes as German pay dispute widens


Nov 23, 13:00


IG Metall called more than 23,000 workers at 19 northern sites to strike for 24 hours. The walkouts hit Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Siemens Gamesa, and Meyer Werft workers were also called out.


A widening dispute in Germany's industrial base could disrupt output and signals labor-cost pressure.


Sources: Euronews Business

entry.title: Afternoon — Nov 23, 2026
entry.content:
PulseBrief's Afternoon Pulse


Mon, Nov 23, 07:00 → Mon, Nov 23, 13:00


Cyber Security


CISA flags Cisco Expressway RCE as exploited; SAP NetWeaver flaw also under attack


Nov 23, 08:44


CISA warned federal agencies that attackers are exploiting a recently patched critical remote code execution flaw in Cisco Expressway. SecurityWeek separately reports that an SAP NetWeaver flaw is being exploited too. The Cisco bug can be used to run commands as root, and the SAP issue can leak or modify server information. The summaries give no attribution or scale of exploitation.


Both are actively exploited in widely deployed enterprise infrastructure, and CISA's flag usually sets a short patching deadline for federal agencies.


Sources: BleepingComputer · SecurityWeek


Critical ASP.NET anti-CSRF library flaw (CVE-2026-131914) exploited for unauthenticated RCE


Nov 23, 10:11


Researchers urge users to stop using the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library after a critical flaw (CVSS 9.3) was found and exploited in the wild. It affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta and allows unauthenticated remote code execution. The summary gives no information on who is exploiting it or how widely.


The library is old and may be buried in legacy ASP.NET apps, so check your dependency inventory for it now.


Sources: The Hacker News


India's CERT-In warns AI-assisted attacks are triggering unauthorized payments at banks and fintechs


Nov 23, 09:24


CERT-In says threat actors are running AI-assisted attacks on ICT assets in India. The activity has led to unauthorized financial transactions at banking and financial services entities and at technology service providers. The summary does not name victims or describe the techniques.


This is a government warning that AI-assisted attacks are already causing real financial losses, not just a theoretical risk.


Sources: The Hacker News


BadBox 3.0 ad-fraud operation generating 40 billion daily bid requests disrupted


Nov 23, 12:44


SecurityWeek reports a disruption of BadBox 3.0, which used backdoors on low-cost consumer devices. The devices served modules for ad fraud and were turned into residential proxies. The operation generated about 40 billion bid requests a day. The summary does not say who carried out the disruption.


Pre-infected cheap devices feeding fraud and proxy networks are a supply-chain threat that can put compromised hardware inside home and corporate networks.


Sources: SecurityWeek


AI & Machine Learning


Z.ai releases GLM-5.4, its first loop transformer (vendor announcement)


Nov 23, 11:06


Z.ai published GLM-5.4, pitched as a step toward generalized coding and built on its first loop transformer architecture. The post drew 992 points and 326 comments on Hacker News, making it one of the most discussed items today. Capability claims come from the vendor and the summary gives no independent benchmarks.


A new architecture from a major Chinese lab for coding models, with heavy developer interest, is a vendor signal worth tracking.


Sources: Z.ai (vendor blog) · Hacker News


Oregon and Virginia sue Musk companies, including SpaceX, over Grok deepfakes


Nov 23, 12:00


The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia are suing several Elon Musk companies, alleging weak safeguards against sexualized imagery of real people, including children. Wired reports the suit names SpaceX. The summary does not give the specific claims or remedies sought.


State-level enforcement over generative AI safeguards is a regulatory precedent that could affect any AI image-generation provider.


Sources: Wired Security


OpenAI customer story names GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna models (vendor content)


Nov 23, 09:00


An OpenAI customer story says Richpanel uses GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol to equip support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT-6 Luna for their conversations. The headline claim is that companies automate 50% of support in 30 days. This is OpenAI marketing, so the results are unverified.


It shows how OpenAI's current model lineup is tiered by role in agent deployments, though the performance claims are the vendor's own.


Sources: OpenAI News (vendor)


Wired essay 'Goodbye, World: The End of Programmers' (opinion)


Nov 23, 11:00


Wired published a first-person essay billed as the last thing the author may ever write about the craft of coding. It is an opinion piece reflecting on AI's effect on programming rather than a news report. The summary gives no data.


It reflects how widely the AI-replacing-coders debate is now framed in mainstream tech media, though it is commentary rather than news.


Sources: Wired AI


Technology


Microsoft confirms printing problems after KB5132043 hotpatch on systems running Forcepoint DLP


Nov 23, 10:11


Microsoft says Windows 11 systems with Forcepoint DLP software have printing issues after the November 2026 KB5132043 hotpatch. The summary does not describe a fix or workaround.


A hotpatch breaking printing on a security-software combination is a rollout risk to check before pushing the update widely.


Sources: BleepingComputer


Airbus plans to leave Microsoft Office in 2-3 years, but not for its 36,000 defense staff


Nov 23, 10:32


The Register reports that Airbus's plan to move off Microsoft's suite stops short of the 22% of staff who cannot work with cloud services. Those are the defense employees, and they will keep Office. The migration is expected to take two to three years.


A large European firm moving away from Microsoft Office signals digital-sovereignty pressure, but the defense carve-out shows its limits.


Sources: The Register


Xfce 4.22 lined up for 2027 as MATE and Xfce push toward Wayland


Nov 23, 11:17


The Register reports that Xfce is planning version 4.22 for 2027. MATE is gaining an Ubuntu-based distribution and its own compositor. Both traditional Linux desktops are finding new routes to Wayland.


It shows the X11-to-Wayland transition reaching even lightweight desktops, which affects Linux desktop deployments.


Sources: The Register


Gentoo developer's 'The next circle of security hell' draws 223 points on Hacker News


Nov 23, 12:34


A post on a Gentoo developer's blog, originally dated Oct 27, is being heavily discussed with 223 points and 131 comments. The summary does not describe its argument, so its content is unconfirmed here.


Attention from open-source maintainers on a security-themed post suggests an ecosystem concern worth reading directly.


Sources: Gentoo blog (mgorny) · Hacker News


Business & Markets


CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in $43.9 billion deal


Nov 23, 12:31


CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion. It expects the combined company to have more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue. The summary does not cover deal terms, regulatory timing or integration plans.


It is a landmark consolidation of endpoint and cloud security vendors that will reshape the market and customer vendor strategies.


Sources: SecurityWeek


Trump urges Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang; Huang to face Congress on Dec 1


Nov 23, 12:44


President Trump has urged Nvidia's board to rehire Huang, joining calls that include a petition with more than 200,000 signatures. The former CEO is due to face questions in Congress on 1 December. This follows Treasury Secretary Bessent's pressure on Nvidia over China chip sales.


Presidential involvement in Nvidia's leadership raises political and regulatory risk for the key AI chip supplier.


Sources: Euronews Business


Capita CEO leaves after pensions contract disaster; shares plunge about 70%


Nov 23, 12:11


The Register reports that outsourcer Capita's CEO is leaving following a pensions contract problem. The company cut profit expectations and plans a £190M cash call, and its shares fell around 70%. The summary does not detail what went wrong in the contract.


A UK public-sector outsourcer collapsing in value is a warning on contract risk for firms that depend on large IT service providers.


Sources: The Register


EU opens new trade defence investigation into Chinese imports


Nov 23, 11:41


The EU investigation could lead to sweeping tariffs or quotas on materials used in defence, renewable energy and transport. Brussels is stepping up efforts to protect European industry from cheap Chinese imports. The summary does not name the specific materials.


Possible new EU tariffs on inputs for strategic sectors could raise costs and reshape supply chains.


Sources: Euronews Business


'Choose France' summit highlights €14.9B in investment; Portugal's tech investment surges after Tekever round


Nov 23, 07:44


The Choose France summit highlights 273 industrial projects worth €14.9 billion, though Euronews notes an undercurrent of uncertainty. Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing two people familiar with the matter, that CrowdStrike is in talks to buy Zscaler. Cybersecurity News relays that the talks are ongoing and could still end without a deal. Neither company has announced anything, and the summary gives no price.


A deal would be a major consolidation of endpoint and cloud security, which would affect vendor choices and contract leverage.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Musk at DealBook on politics, a potential merger and Ukraine


Nov 21, 14:00


Elon Musk spoke with Andrew Ross Sorkin at the DealBook Summit, covering his politics, a potential merger and Ukraine. The summary does not say which companies a merger would involve or what he said about it. He is chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX.


Any comment on a merger involving Musk's companies is market-moving, so check the full interview for specifics.


Sources: NYT Business


NYT explains how the US economy is tied to AI, and the risk in that


Nov 21, 16:06


In a video explainer, NYT chief economics correspondent Ben Casselman describes how AI has become a huge piece of the US economy and why that could be risky. It comes the day after the S&P 500 fell into correction on AI spending worries. The summary gives no figures.


It explains the exposure behind this week's market slide, which affects funding and valuations across tech.


Sources: NYT Business


Nvidia: new detail on Huang's culture of humiliation and interim CEO Kress's all-hands


Nov 21, 15:31


NYT adds reporting that Jensen Huang's belittling of employees goes back decades and once led to a confidential settlement with an executive who said he was 'terrorized'. A second NYT piece covers what interim CEO Colette Kress told employees at an all-hands meeting after Huang's resignation. She sought to put his indiscretions behind the company. This builds on earlier culture reporting and the SEC and California subpoena scrutiny.


The governance story at the key AI chip supplier is still deepening, and the interim leadership's message shows how it is trying to steady the company.


Sources: NYT Technology (culture) · NYT Technology (Kress)

entry.content:
PulseBrief's Afternoon Pulse


Sat, Nov 21, 07:00 → Sat, Nov 21, 13:00


Cyber Security


CISA adds VMware vCenter, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and Apache Roller flaws to its exploited-vulnerabilities list


Nov 21, 09:49


CISA added four flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Friday, citing evidence of active exploitation. They affect Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and Broadcom VMware vCenter, and one carries a CVSS score of 9.8. The vCenter and Expressway entries follow earlier reports of China-linked and PoC-driven exploitation.


A KEV listing sets federal patch deadlines and confirms exploitation, so any of these four products in your estate should move to the front of the queue.


Sources: The Hacker News


GnuPG warns of critical GPGME flaw: a malicious OpenPGP key can expose application data


Nov 21, 09:32


The GnuPG project says a malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the library most programs use to work with GnuPG. The flaw (CVE-2026-129975) could be used to steal data from affected applications. It affects all software using GPGME before version 2.3.0, and fixed versions are out. The GnuPG announcement was also the subject of a Hacker News thread titled 'RCE in Gnupg' (166 points).


GPGME sits underneath many mail and signing tools, so check which of your applications bundle it and update to 2.3.0 or later.


Sources: The Hacker News · GnuPG announce list


FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database


Nov 21, 11:33


The BBC reports that the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal database. The thread drew 136 points and 70 comments on Hacker News. The summary gives no detail on what data was reached, who is responsible, or how access was gained.


If confirmed, a compromise of a core law-enforcement system is a major incident, and it lands in a week of unexplained outages and the departure of the national cyber director.


Sources: BBC News · Hacker News


Detail emerges on the AI-agent zero-day: MONAI Label flaw gave root on a university server (vendor research)


Nov 21, 12:03


Amazon Threat Intelligence says suspected China-linked attackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server. The bug lets an unauthenticated attacker write files outside the server's storage folder, and it affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier in the default setup. The attackers gained root on a university server. The findings come from Amazon's own research.


This confirms the exposed product and the exploit class for the first documented case of AI agents finding and exploiting a zero-day, so anyone running MONAI Label has a concrete patch target.


Sources: The Hacker News


AI & Machine Learning


One malicious webpage let researchers hijack Meta Muse and read private chats and memories


Nov 21, 12:53


Researchers showed that a malicious webpage could extract a Muse user's private conversations and stored memories without triggering any approval prompt. The same attack could be extended to reach credentials Muse stores for connected accounts. It was a laboratory demonstration, not an attack on real users.


It is another agent permission failure in Muse, following earlier reports of the assistant leaking users' private data, and it shows the risk of assistants that hold credentials.


Sources: The Hacker News


Signal restricts screenshots by default to keep AI agents out of chats, but admits protection is 'incomplete' (vendor action)


Nov 21, 09:49


Signal will block screenshots by default on iOS 27, where agentic systems are built into the OS, and on Android versions where it can detect an AI assistant trying to read the screen. Signal itself concedes that the protection is 'incomplete'. This is Signal's own announcement.


A major encrypted messenger is openly treating OS-level AI agents as a threat, and its admission of gaps shows how hard that threat is to contain.


Sources: The Hacker News


ChatGPT shrunk down to run on a Super Nintendo


Nov 21, 12:46


The Register reports that a hobbyist version of a ChatGPT-style model has been squeezed onto a Super Nintendo. Don't expect complex, coherent, or always correct answers. It is a novelty project, with no practical use claimed.


It is a light signal of how far model compression can go, though the output quality makes it a curiosity.


Sources: The Register


Technology


NYT analysis: AI-driven outages and attacks fit a historical pattern of innovation causing failure first


Nov 21, 11:02


The NYT argues that if AI is contributing to this week's outages and cyberattacks, it fits history, where new technologies often cause calamitous failures before they improve life. It is analysis rather than new reporting, and no cause for the outages has been confirmed. It lands in the middle of the debate over AI-accelerated patching.


It frames the week's run of outages for a mainstream audience, but it does not establish AI as the cause.


Sources: NYT Technology


NASA's Mars rover and orbiter both suffer glitches


Nov 21, 08:47


The Register reports that NASA's Mars rover and an orbiter have each hit technical problems. The summary gives no detail on the severity, the cause or the impact on missions.


It is a reminder that the week's technical failures are not confined to Earth, though the scale of the problems is unclear.


Sources: The Register


A monitor was cutting one user's download speed by 75%


Nov 21, 11:36


A blog post tracing a slow connection to a display's built-in Ethernet drew 274 points and 129 comments on Hacker News. It describes the monitor as the cause of a 75% drop in download speed. The summary gives no further technical detail.


It is a practical troubleshooting case that is widely read by developers, and it is worth a look if you use docks or displays with built-in networking.


Sources: tymscar blog · Hacker News


Business & Markets


Anthropic's record IPO meets a rocky first full trading day as markets slide on AI spending worries


Nov 21, 11:03


NYT reports that Anthropic broke records with its initial public offering this week, then had a rocky first full day of trading as markets plunged on worries about AI spending. It describes a disconnect between Wall Street and Silicon Valley. This follows the S&P 500 entering correction territory on Friday.


The market is separating the success of one AI listing from doubts about the wider AI buildout, which affects funding and valuations across the sector.


Sources: NYT Business


EU's Costa cuts proposed budget by €44B and plans a Big Tech tax


Nov 21, 11:44


Politico reports that European Council President António Costa has cut the proposed EU budget by €44 billion. Brussels plans a tax on Big Tech to raise billions for the next budget cycle. The summary gives no rate or scope for the tax.


A new EU levy aimed at large technology companies is a regulatory signal, though the design is still unknown.


Sources: Politico EU


Electric truck maker Harbinger raises $240M Series D, backed by a $300M FedEx order and a military contract


Nov 21, 13:00


Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D round earlier this month, according to The Verge. The company also has a $300 million FedEx order and a new US military contract. It focuses on Class 4-6 delivery vans and box trucks, skipping consumer EVs.


It is a funding round above $50 million that shows capital going to commercial EVs while legacy automakers pull back.


Sources: The Verge


Von der Leyen says Russian threats are 'less and less hybrid' after Denmark thwarts an assassination plot


Nov 21, 12:43


Danish authorities said they thwarted a Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian rapper in September. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that Russian threats are becoming 'less and less hybrid'. The summary gives no detail on how the plot was foiled.


It signals a rising Russian threat in Europe, which affects security posture and risk assessments for companies operating there.


Sources: Politico EU
